rules.t: Unarmed strikes with smite, sneak attack and styles
rules.k: unarmed strike smite sneak attack dueling monk paladin fist weapon
rules.s: An unarmed strike is a melee weapon attack, but not a weapon. Sneak Attack and Savage Attacker need a weapon, so they do not apply (official). The same reasoning is usually applied to Divine Smite and the Dueling style, though the Compendium does not rule on those.
b: Stunning Strike works (it needs a melee weapon attack).
Booming Blade and Green-Flame Blade need a weapon worth at least 1 sp.

rules.k: twin twinned metamagic sorcerer target one creature eligible dragons breath haste
rules.s: Only a spell that targets one creature and is incapable of targeting more at the level you cast it, and not Self range.
b: Sage Advice rules out spells that can target an object, let you pick more than one creature, can force saves from more than one creature over their duration (Dragon's Breath), or involve a roll that can affect more than one.
Eligible: Haste, Polymorph, Hold Person at 2nd level, Disintegrate (strictly no, it can target objects; many DMs allow it).
Not eligible: Fireball, Chaos Bolt, Ice Knife, Eldritch Blast at level 5+, Green-Flame Blade, any spell upcast to add targets.
rules.d: The "can target an object" exclusion rules out Fire Bolt too by the official list. Most tables ignore that part; pick one and write it down.

rules.t: Wild Shape and Polymorph hit points
rules.k: wild shape polymorph hit points zero revert carry over damage concentration beast
rules.s: You take on the new form's hit points. At 0 you revert to your own hit points as they were, and any leftover damage carries over.
b: If the carried damage drops your own form to 0, you fall unconscious as normal.
A druid keeps concentrating on spells in Wild Shape, and can keep one going, but cannot cast new ones until 18th level.
Polymorph replaces mental scores too; Wild Shape keeps yours.
Instant-death and "if this reduces you to 0" effects apply to the form, then you revert.

rules.k: haste extra action attack one weapon dash disengage hide cast
rules.s: One of: Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide or Use an Object. Not casting a spell, and no Extra Attack on it.
b: When it ends you lose a whole turn: you cannot move or take actions until after your next turn.

rules.k: jump spell boots striding springing speed limit movement
rules.s: Every foot jumped uses a foot of your movement, so you cannot jump farther than the movement you have left, even with the Jump spell.
b: Dash gives more movement to jump with.

rules.k: lucky feat disadvantage three dice choose super advantage
rules.s: With disadvantage you roll two dice, spend a luck point for a third, and choose any of the three. Official ruling, and yes, it is better than plain advantage.
rules.d: A common house rule: Lucky replaces the die you would have used, so disadvantage still takes the lower of the remaining pair.

rules.t: You can see the invisible creature. Does it still get advantage?
rules.k: see invisibility truesight faerie fire invisible advantage still condition raw
rules.s: By the text, yes: the invisible condition grants advantage and imposes disadvantage whether or not you can see it. Faerie Fire is different because it says the creature gains no benefit from being invisible.
b: This is a designer comment on the wording, not an official ruling. Most tables rule that if you can see it, the advantage and disadvantage go away.
rules.d: Pick the sensible reading (seeing it cancels the benefit) and record it under House rules.
rules.n24: Settled in the text: if a creature can somehow see you, you gain no attack benefit against that creature.

rules.t: Magic Missile: damage rolls and concentration
rules.k: magic missile darts one roll concentration checks each missile hex empowered evocation
rules.s: The darts strike at once. The designers have said to roll the damage once and use it for every dart, and that a concentrating target saves separately for each dart that hits it.
b: Rolling per dart is how most tables play it.
With one roll, Empowered Evocation adds Intelligence to every dart.
rules.d: This is commentary, not a Sage Advice ruling. Either way is defensible: choose one.

rules.k: shield magic missile immune negate
rules.s: Shield says you take no damage from Magic Missile. It is cast as a reaction when you are targeted, and blocks every dart aimed at you.

rules.t: Countering a Counterspell on your own turn
rules.k: counterspell counter own turn bonus action spell blocked reaction
rules.s: Allowed: a reaction can be used on your own turn. But if you cast a bonus-action spell that turn you cannot, because the only other spell allowed is a 1-action cantrip.
b: So: Fireball, enemy Counterspells, you Counterspell that: fine. Healing Word then Fire Bolt, enemy Counterspells: you cannot respond.
rules.n24: The limit is one spell slot per turn, so you cannot cast a slot spell and then Counterspell with another slot on the same turn.

rules.k: subtle spell counterspell no components see casting material
rules.s: Counterspell needs you to see the casting. A Subtle spell with no material component has nothing to see.
b: If it has a material component, the caster still handles it and can be seen.

rules.t: Shield Master: shove before or after attacking?
rules.k: shield master shove bonus action before attack prone timing
rules.s: After. The bonus shove needs you to "take the Attack action", and the ruling since 2019 is that you must finish that action (all its attacks) first.
b: Before 2018 the designers said the opposite, so many tables still allow the shove first.
rules.d: Same logic for any "if you take the X action, you can…" bonus action without its own timing.

rules.k: war caster opportunity attack spell reaction booming blade eldritch blast one target
rules.s: Instead of the melee attack you can cast a spell at the creature: casting time 1 action, targeting only that creature.
b: Booming Blade works. Eldritch Blast works but every beam must go at that creature. Fireball does not (area, not a single target).
The creature is leaving your reach when you cast, so it is still within reach for touch and melee-range spells.

rules.k: booming blade move willingly pushed forced shove dissonant whispers fear
rules.s: The extra damage triggers only if the target "willingly moves". Being shoved, pulled or thrown does not count.
b: Booming Blade and Green-Flame Blade use the Cast a Spell action: no Extra Attack, and no opportunity attack unless a feature such as War Caster allows it (official).
Dissonant Whispers makes the target move with its reaction, so that movement provokes opportunity attacks (official).
Whether magically compelled movement (Dissonant Whispers, Command, fleeing in fear) is "willing" has no official ruling: the DM decides.

rules.t: Spirit Guardians, Moonbeam and "enters the area"
rules.k: spirit guardians moonbeam wall of fire enters first time on a turn drag push area cast on top
rules.s: Creating the area on top of creatures does not count as them entering it. They are affected when they enter it or start their turn there.
b: Moving the area onto a creature (walking with Spirit Guardians) is also not entering.
Being pushed or dragged into it does count, but only the first time on each turn.
So the same creature can be hurt on several different turns in one round if allies keep moving it in.

rules.t: Smiting with a punch or an improvised weapon
rules.src: PHB ch.3 wording; no official ruling found
rules.k: smite unarmed improvised weapon fist paladin
rules.s: Divine Smite adds to "the weapon's damage", and an unarmed strike is not a weapon, so most tables say no to smiting with a fist. The Compendium has no ruling on it: the DM decides. An improvised weapon is a weapon, so it works.

rules.k: heavy armor master reduce 3 resistance order rage half
rules.s: Reductions apply before resistance. A raging barbarian with Heavy Armor Master taking 15 slashing: (15 − 3) ÷ 2 = 6.

rules.t: Disintegrate, Power Word Kill and a shapechanged target
rules.k: disintegrate wild shape polymorph zero dust power word kill form hit points
rules.s: Disintegrate on a wild-shaped druid: the druid leaves beast form, leftover damage applies to the normal form, and the druid is disintegrated only if that leaves the normal form at 0.
b: Power Word Kill checks the current form's hit points (100 or fewer), and kills outright.
Effects that reduce a hit point maximum carry back to the true form only if they say so.
rules.d: This is the current official answer (2020). The 2017 version said the literal text turned the druid to dust and called this reading the intent.

rules.t: Casting at a target the spell cannot affect
rules.k: invalid target wasted slot hold person on undead charm immune know
rules.s: Xanathar's: if you target something the spell cannot affect, nothing happens to it but the slot is still spent. If the spell normally allows a save, it appears the target simply succeeded.
b: So casting Hold Person on a disguised fiend looks like a made save.

rules.k: feather fall reaction fall instantly 500 feet turn
rules.s: Feather Fall is a reaction when you or a creature within 60 feet falls, so it can be cast before impact even on someone else's turn. With Xanathar's optional rule a fall covers 500 feet at once, so longer falls give time for other answers.

rules.k: darkness spell devils sight darkvision magical cant see through light dispel
rules.s: Darkvision cannot see through magical Darkness; Devil's Sight and truesight can. Nonmagical light does not illuminate it, and a light spell of 2nd level or lower is dispelled where they overlap.
b: A warlock inside it with Devil's Sight attacks with advantage and is attacked with disadvantage, but so are their blinded allies.
If the object it was cast on is covered, the darkness is blocked.

rules.k: grapple teleport misty step thunderwave break free dimension door carried
rules.s: A grapple ends when something moves the grappled creature out of the grappler's reach. Misty Step works (it has only a verbal component and does not need movement speed), and a push such as Thunderwave breaks it too.
b: Dimension Door can bring one willing creature along; a grappler is not willing.

rules.k: ready attack extra attack one swing not your turn
rules.s: Extra Attack works only on your turn, so a readied Attack is a single attack. A readied cantrip keeps its full damage.

rules.t: Assassinate when the target wins initiative
rules.k: assassin assassinate surprised crit initiative lost target acted
rules.s: A surprised creature stops being surprised at the end of its first turn. If it rolled higher than the assassin, its (empty) turn has passed and the automatic critical hit is gone. Advantage against creatures that have not yet acted follows the same order.
rules.n24: Surprise is only disadvantage on initiative, so the 2014 timing problem does not come up.

rules.t: Sentinel against Disengage and Polearm Master
rules.k: sentinel disengage speed zero polearm master reach stop
rules.s: Sentinel lets you make opportunity attacks even against Disengage, and a hit sets the target's speed to 0 for the turn.
b: With Polearm Master, a creature entering your 10-foot reach can be stopped there, out of its own reach.
Sentinel's third benefit needs the attacker to be within 5 feet of you.

rules.k: magical antimagic dispel breath weapon dragon wild shape ki check list
rules.s: The official test: it is magical if it is a magic item, a spell or lets you cast one, a spell attack, fueled by spell slots, or its description says it is magical.
b: By that test a dragon's breath is not magical, and Wild Shape is (its text says you magically assume the shape).
Only magical things are stopped by Antimagic Field or resisted by Magic Resistance.

rules.t: Things that happen at the same time
rules.k: simultaneous same time order start of turn end choose who decides
rules.s: Xanathar's: when several things happen at the same moment on a creature's turn, the creature whose turn it is (the player, or the DM for a monster) chooses the order.
b: Example: Regeneration and ongoing damage at the start of a turn.

rules.k: xanathar ten rules basics remember summary exceptions round down same name reaction bonus action spell concentration temp hp
rules.s: Exceptions beat general rules; round down; advantage and disadvantage do not stack; proficiency is added once; same-named effects do not stack; one bonus action; bonus-action spell means only a cantrip otherwise; one reaction; concentrate on one spell; temporary hit points do not stack.

rules.k: time round six seconds minute hour day how long scale dungeon travel
rules.s: A round is 6 seconds, so 10 rounds are a minute. Dungeon exploring runs in minutes, town and wilderness in hours, long journeys in days.
b: About a minute to creep down a long hallway, another to check a door for traps, ten to search a room.
Effects that last "1 minute" are 10 rounds; "1 hour" outlasts almost any single fight.
rules.d: Track time loosely outside combat. It matters for spell durations, torches and wandering monsters.

rules.k: ability scores generate roll 4d6 drop lowest standard array point buy 27
rules.s: Roll 4d6 and drop the lowest, six times. Or use the standard array: 15, 14, 13, 12, 10, 8. Or point buy with 27 points (optional).
b: Point buy: scores from 8 to 15 before racial bonuses. 8 costs 0, 9 = 1, 10 = 2, 11 = 3, 12 = 4, 13 = 5, 14 = 7, 15 = 9.
Racial increases come after.

rules.k: language common dwarvish elvish exotic draconic thieves cant druidic speak read
rules.s: Your race and background give your languages. Standard ones are free to choose; exotic ones need the DM's permission.
b: Standard: Common, Dwarvish, Elvish, Giant, Gnomish, Goblin, Halfling, Orc.
Exotic: Abyssal, Celestial, Draconic, Deep Speech, Infernal, Primordial, Sylvan, Undercommon.
Primordial has four dialects (Auran, Aquan, Ignan, Terran); speakers of one understand the others.
Thieves' cant and Druidic are secret languages from class features.

rules.k: school abjuration conjuration divination enchantment evocation illusion necromancy transmutation
rules.s: Eight schools sort spells by kind. They have no rules of their own; features and items refer to them.
b: Abjuration protects. Conjuration brings or moves things. Divination reveals. Enchantment sways minds.
Evocation makes energy. Illusion deceives the senses. Necromancy works with life and death. Transmutation changes things.

rules.k: duration instantaneous until dispelled concentration end early dismiss
rules.s: Instantaneous spells happen and are done: they cannot be dispelled afterward. Others last their stated time, or until concentration ends.
b: You can end your own concentration spell at any time, no action needed.
A non-concentration spell with a duration runs its full time unless it says you can dismiss it.
Dispel Magic cannot undo an instantaneous spell's result (the damage done, the creature raised).

rules.k: interact object lever door pull push break open stuck check environment
rules.s: Say what you do; the DM says what happens. A check is only needed when something is stuck, heavy, hidden or dangerous.
b: Forcing a stuck door or a jammed lever is usually a Strength check.
Characters can also damage objects: see Breaking objects.

rules.k: horse mount vehicle carry pull wagon ship speed barding saddle rowing
rules.s: A mount can carry its normal capacity; pulling a cart, it moves five times that weight (including the cart). A good mount covers ground faster for a while but not much farther in a day.
b: Barding is armor for a mount: it costs four times the same armor for a humanoid and weighs twice as much.
An exotic or military saddle helps you stay mounted; a military saddle gives advantage on checks to remain in it.
Waterborne vehicles keep their own pace and do not tire: a ship can travel 24 hours a day with a crew.
Rowed boats move 1½ miles an hour; a sailing ship about 2; a galley about 4.

rules.k: wear two rings cloaks boots pair gloves slots how many magic items same kind
rules.s: One pair of footwear, one pair of gloves, one pair of bracers, one suit of armor, one headwear and one cloak. Paired items work only when you wear both of the pair.
b: The DM can allow exceptions that make sense (a circlet under a helmet).
Most worn items resize to fit. There is no set limit on rings or amulets beyond attunement and common sense.

rules.k: silver silvered weapon werewolf resistance nonmagical adamantine cost
rules.s: Silvering one weapon or ten pieces of ammunition costs 100 gp. It gets past resistance or immunity to nonmagical attacks for monsters that are weak to silver.
b: A magic weapon gets past "nonmagical attacks" resistance for every monster.

rules.k: healers kit stabilize uses medicine bandage first aid
rules.s: Ten uses. As an action, spend one to stabilize a creature at 0 hit points, with no check needed.
b: Without a kit: Wisdom (Medicine) DC 10.
It does not restore hit points (the Healer feat changes that).

rules.k: sentient intelligent item sword talks conflict control personality
rules.s: A sentient item has Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma, senses, an alignment and a purpose. If its wielder acts against that, it can make demands or try to take control.
b: Control: the wielder makes a Charisma save, DC 12 + the item's Charisma modifier. On a failure they are charmed by it for 1d12 hours and must try to follow its commands; taking damage allows a new save.
It can also refuse to work, suppress its properties or block attunement to other items.
rules.d: Play it as an NPC with its own goals, run by you.

rules.k: stat block hit dice size monster saving throws skills challenge proficiency read
rules.s: A monster's Hit Die depends on its size: Tiny d4, Small d6, Medium d8, Large d10, Huge d12, Gargantuan d20. Listed saves and skills already include its proficiency bonus.
b: Hit points are the average; you can roll them instead.
If a save or skill is not listed, use the bare ability modifier.
Armor, weapons and spells in the block are part of the monster; changing them changes its numbers.

rules.k: blindsight darkvision tremorsense truesight telepathy senses range
rules.s: Blindsight perceives without sight in its radius. Tremorsense pinpoints vibrations through the same ground, not flying or incorporeal creatures. Truesight sees through darkness, invisibility, illusions and shape changes.
b: Darkvision: sees in darkness as if dim light, in shades of gray, within range.
Truesight also sees into the Ethereal Plane within range, and automatically succeeds on saves against visual illusions.
Telepathy lets a creature speak mind to mind within range; the other need not share a language but must understand at least one.
A creature hidden from sight is not hidden from blindsight or tremorsense within range.

rules.k: type aberration beast celestial construct dragon elemental fey fiend giant humanoid monstrosity ooze plant undead
rules.s: Fourteen types: aberration, beast, celestial, construct, dragon, elemental, fey, fiend, giant, humanoid, monstrosity, ooze, plant, undead. A type has no rules of its own, but spells and features care about it.
b: Hold Person and Charm Person only work on humanoids. Turn Undead only on undead.
Polymorph and Wild Shape need a beast.
Tags in brackets (goblinoid, shapechanger, devil) work the same way.

rules.k: swarm rats insects occupy space squeeze heal temporary hit points
rules.s: A swarm can occupy another creature's space and the reverse, and can squeeze through any opening big enough for one of its members. It cannot regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.
b: Swarms resist bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, and are immune to most conditions that target one body (grappled, prone, restrained, stunned and others).
Its attack usually deals less damage at half hit points or fewer.

rules.k: poison contact ingested inhaled injury apply weapon dose
rules.s: Contact: touching it is enough. Ingested: a full dose must be swallowed. Inhaled: fills a 5-foot cube; holding your breath does not help. Injury: on a weapon or needle, it works on a hit and stays potent until delivered or washed off.
b: Each poison has its own Constitution save DC and effect.

presets.text:
When you and at least one ally are next to the same enemy on opposite sides of it (opposite squares or opposite corners), you each have advantage on melee attack rolls against it.
You can't flank an enemy you can't see, or while you are incapacitated.
On a grid, the first diagonal square you move costs 5 feet, the second 10 feet, the third 5 feet, and so on. Count range the same way. Distances come out closer to real ones.
A short rest takes 8 hours and a long rest takes 7 days. Fights and travel wear the party down; good for grim or slow-paced campaigns.
A short rest takes 5 minutes and a long rest takes 1 hour. The party recovers quickly and can face more fights in a day.
You don't regain hit points at the end of a long rest. Instead, you can spend Hit Dice to heal at the end of a long rest, just as after a short rest.
You can't spend Hit Dice after a short rest until someone spends one use of a healer's kit to bandage and treat your wounds.

When a creature takes damage from a single source equal to or more than half its hit point maximum, it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or suffer a random effect from the DMG's System Shock table.

When your melee attack drops an undamaged creature to 0 hit points, the leftover damage can carry over: pick another creature within your reach, and if the same attack roll would hit it, it takes the leftover damage. If that drops another undamaged creature, keep going.
Instead of adding your proficiency bonus, roll a die: +2 is 1d4, +3 is 1d6, +4 is 1d8, +5 is 1d10, +6 is 1d12. When a feature doubles your proficiency bonus, roll the die twice.

You start with 5 hero points at 1st level. Each time you gain a level, unspent points are lost and you get 5 plus half your level.
After you roll a d20 for an attack, ability check or saving throw (before you know the result), you can spend one to roll a d6 and add it. When you fail a death saving throw, you can spend one to make it a success.

presets.t: Drinking a potion is a bonus action
presets.src: Table custom (not in the 2014 books; the 2024 rules make it a bonus action)
presets.text: Drinking a potion yourself takes a bonus action. Giving a potion to another creature still takes an action.

presets.t: Critical hits: the extra dice count as maximum
presets.text: On a critical hit, roll your damage dice as usual and add the highest possible total of those dice once more, instead of rolling them twice.

presets.t: Level-up hit points: never below the fixed value
presets.text: When you gain a level, roll your Hit Die for hit points; if the roll is lower than the fixed value (half the die plus 1), take the fixed value instead.
The DM rolls death saving throws for dying characters out of sight, so nobody at the table knows how close the end is.
When you roll a 1 on the d20 for an attack, ability check or saving throw, you gain Inspiration.

presets.src: Table custom (not in the books; both apps can hide the others in Settings)
presets.text: Spellcasters don't track material components unless the spell gives them a gold cost or uses them up. Verbal and somatic components still count.
